original_question: Let M be a model, let T be a tree that is Π0_1(∅′) in M, and suppose there exists g ∈ [T] such that M[g] |= BΣ2. Must there exist a definable path h ∈ [T] such that M[h] |= BΣ2?
target_in_paper: Section 9 (Chong Chi Tat), Problem 31, introduced immediately after Problem 30 as the paper’s "Tree version" and stated as the n = 2 case on page 14. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official target almost exactly: it has a model M, a tree T that is Π^0_1(∅′) in M, an existing path g ∈ [T] with M[g] ⊨ BΣ_2, and asks whether there must be a definable path h ∈ [T] with M[h] ⊨ BΣ_2. That is essentially Problem 31 verbatim. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The ambient theory on M is omitted. In the immediately preceding setup for Problem 30, the paper assumes M ⊨ RCA_0 + BΣ_n + ¬IΣ_n; it then says, "Tree version: Without loss of generality, let us state the problem for n = 2," so the intended background for Problem 31 is the n = 2 instance, namely M ⊨ RCA_0 + BΣ_2 + ¬IΣ_2. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The draft says "definable path," but the nearby official wording makes the definability internal to M (Problem 30 asks for a choice function "definable in M"). A stand-alone restatement should therefore say that h is definable in M. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should say that T is a tree coded in/over M and that [T] denotes the set of infinite paths through T; the paper uses this notation without re-defining it at Problem 31. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The draft suppresses the fact that Problem 31 is not an isolated neighboring question but the paper’s tree reformulation of Problem 30. Mentioning that linkage keeps the scope exactly aligned with the paper. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For complete standalone notation, one may also spell out that M[g] denotes the extension of the reverse-mathematical model M obtained by adjoining the path g; this is an inferential unpacking of the paper’s notation rather than an extra hypothesis. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let M be a model of RCA_0 + BΣ_2 + ¬IΣ_2, and let T be a tree coded in M that is Π^0_1(∅′) over M. Suppose there exists a path g ∈ [T] such that the extension M[g] obtained by adjoining g satisfies BΣ_2. Must there exist a path h ∈ [T] that is definable in M and such that M[h] also satisfies BΣ_2? ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
equivalent_formulation: General choice-function version on the same page: let M be a model satisfying RCA_0 + BΣ_n + ¬IΣ_n. Fix a Π_n subset X of M, and suppose ⟨A_s : s ∈ M⟩ is a sequence of pairwise disjoint M-finite sets such that A_s ∩ X ≠ ∅ for every s. Is there a choice function f, definable in M, such that f(s) ∈ A_s ∩ X for all s? The paper then says that, without loss of generality, this can be stated in the tree form for n = 2 as Problem 31. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The nearest official target is Problem 31 itself, not a broader surrounding issue. Your draft already matches that statement very closely, so the only sharpening needed is to restore the ambient assumptions inherited from Problem 30 and to make explicit that the desired branch is definable in M. I therefore kept the question in the paper’s own n = 2 tree form rather than replacing it by a more general or neighboring problem. ([tianyuan.amss.ac.cn](https://tianyuan.amss.ac.cn/upload/fab78d36-bd52-42eb-84d3-ff99c953bb08/20250708/67111751937959724.pdf?utm_source=openai))
